newsitem.title: UK: LIFFE white sugar climbs off lows but spreads flat.
newsitem.headline: LIFFE white sugar climbs off lows but spreads flat.

text.p: White sugar futures picked up from their earlier lows in listless Tuesday trading but steady movements across the board kept both the nearby spreads and the March white premium in tandem, traders said on Tuesday.

The spot March contract avoided even making an attempt to approach $300.00 resistance after its brief upward foray on Monday, but light mixed buying kept it above nearby support at $296.00 despite a quick visit to $295.10. "There's a little bit of support coming back into the market after this morning's dive," said one trader.
"I think people were thinking it might go through support but it held up."
At 1727 GMT March was down 90 cents at $297.00, the same level as May and August, which were down 70 cents at $2.30 respectively. Volume totalled 929 lots.
Traders said the flat spreads for the three nearby months would probably deter buyers with non-urgent demand as they could hold off at least until the start of 1997.
The March white/raw premium narrowed slightly to around $69 and with the generally bearish sentiment in London, more selling is widely expected on the whites to drag it down further.
In the physical market, there was conflicting news about the results of Pakistan's recent tender to buy 50,000 tonnes of crystal whites.
London traders cited a purchase in two rail consignments at $360.00 per tonne c&f, while Pakistan's state-run TCP said a decision would not be made until December 12.
The pattern was similar on the Paris futures market where 477 lots were traded. March was down $2.00 at $297.00 and May was down by the same amount at $296.50.
